Normalize Workflows and Analyze Requirements\n+\n+Implement a workflow loading layer that converts raw template files into a consistent API workflow representation.\n+\n+Core functions:\n+\n+```python\n+load_template(path) -> RawWorkflow\n+normalize_to_api(raw) -> ApiWorkflowDict\n+analyze_requirements(api_workflow) -> WorkflowRequirements\n+```\n+\n+CLI target:\n+\n+```bash\n+vibecomfy inspect <template-id>\n+vibecomfy inspect vendor/workflow_templates/.../some_template.json\n+```\n+\n+Output should include:\n+\n+```text\n+nodes: N\n+custom nodes: [...]\n+models: [...]\n+input knobs: prompt, seed, width, height, steps...\n+output nodes: SaveImage / VHS_VideoCombine / ...\n+status: runnable | missing_nodes | missing_models | unsupported\n+```\n+\n+Use HiddenSwitch's `comfyui workflow-requirements` path where possible. If it cannot be called as a library, wrap it carefully and capture structured output.\n+\n+Deliverables:\n+\n+- `vibecomfy/templates/loader.py`\n+- `vibecomfy/templates/normalize.py`\n+- `vibecomfy/runtime/requirements.py`\n+- `vibecomfy inspect`\n+\n+Acceptance check:\n+\n+```bash\n+vibecomfy inspect --all --limit 20\n+```\n+\n+Pass condition:\n+\n+- No parser crashes.\n+- Every inspected template is classified as `runnable`, `missing_models`, `missing_nodes`, or `unsupported`.\n+- Missing model and missing custom-node messages are readable.\n+\n+## 5. Build the JSON Passthrough Runner First\n+\n+The fastest useful product is a reliable runner for existing Comfy workflow JSON. Build this before attempting beautiful Python export.\n+\n+Execution path:\n+\n+```text\n+template JSON -> normalized API dict -> patch values -> queue_prompt -> outputs\n+```\n+\n+Target API:\n+\n+```python\n+from vibecomfy import Template, run\n+\n+template = Template.from_id(\"flux_txt2img\")\n+workflow = (\n+    template\n+    .patch(\"positive_prompt\", \"a cinematic robot painter\")\n+    .patch(\"steps\", 20)\n+    .patch(\"seed\", 123)\n+    .build()\n+)\n+\n+outputs = await run(workflow)\n+```\n+\n+CLI targets:\n+\n+```bash\n+vibecomfy patch <template-id> --prompt \"red glass dragon\" --seed 42 --steps 8 --out workflow.json\n+vibecomfy run workflow.json\n+```\n+\n+Runtime output requirements:\n+\n+- Output files saved to a predictable directory.\n+- Metadata saved with prompt, seed, template id, workflow hash, and git SHA.\n+- Runtime logs captured per run.\n+- Queue errors surfaced with the relevant missing model or node name.\n+\n+Deliverables:\n+\n+- `vibecomfy/templates/template.py`\n+- `vibecomfy/templates/patch.py`\n+- `vibecomfy/runtime/client.py`\n+- `vibecomfy/runtime/run.py`\n+- `vibecomfy patch`\n+- `vibecomfy run`\n+\n+Acceptance check:\n+\n+Run one simple SDXL or FLUX text-to-image workflow through JSON passthrough and confirm an output file exists.\n+\n+## 6. Add the GraphBuilder Compiler and Python Export Path\n+\n+Build this as a second path after JSON passthrough works. The first version should prioritize lossless round-tripping and executable output over elegant generated code.\n+\n+Compiler paths:\n+\n+```text\n+A. JSON passthrough:\n+   template JSON -> normalized API dict -> queue_prompt\n+\n+B. Python builder:\n+   template JSON -> intermediate graph IR -> GraphBuilder Python function -> workflow dict -> queue_prompt\n+```\n+\n+Target API:\n+\n+```python\n+workflow = (\n+    Template.from_id(\"flux_txt2img\")\n+    .patch(\"positive_prompt\", \"a cinematic robot painter\")\n+    .patch(\"steps\", 20)\n+    .patch(\"seed\", 123)\n+    .to_graphbuilder()\n+    .build()\n+)\n+```\n+\n+Support custom code on top:\n+\n+```python\n+def make_variations(base_template, prompts):\n+    for prompt in prompts:\n+        yield base_template.patch(\"positive_prompt\", prompt).build()\n+```\n+\n+CLI target:\n+\n+```bash\n+vibecomfy export-python <template-id> --out examples/<template-id>.py\n+python examples/<template-id>.py --dry-run\n+python examples/<template-id>.py --run\n+```\n+\n+Deliverables:\n+\n+- `vibecomfy/graphbuilder/ir.py`\n+- `vibecomfy/graphbuilder/compiler.py`\n+- `vibecomfy/graphbuilder/export_python.py`\n+- `vibecomfy export-python`\n+\n+Acceptance check:\n+\n+- Export at least five templates to Python.\n+- The generated Python can rebuild a workflow dict accepted by `queue_prompt`.\n+- At least three GraphBuilder outputs execute successfully.\n+\n+Risk note:\n+\n+- Do not block the project on perfectly translating every Comfy workflow into hand-crafted Python. Make the compiler correct first, then improve readability template by template.\n+\n+## 7. Design the Scratchpad API and CLI\n+\n+The scratchpad is the user-facing Python layer for starting from a known template and modifying it with code.\n+\n+Target API:\n+\n+```python\n+from vibecomfy import Scratchpad\n+\n+pad = Scratchpad(\"wan_txt2video\")\n+pad.replace_prompt(\"a floating crystal city at sunrise\")\n+pad.set_model(\"wan2.1\")\n+pad.add_node(\"KJNodes.SomeNode\", ...)\n+pad.connect(...)\n+workflow = pad.compile()\n+```\n+\n+Minimum CLI commands:\n+\n+```bash\n+vibecomfy list-templates\n+vibecomfy inspect <template-id>\n+vibecomfy patch <template-id> --prompt \"...\" --seed 1 --out workflow.json\n+vibecomfy run workflow.json\n+vibecomfy export-python <template-id> --out examples/foo.py\n+vibecomfy smoke\n+```\n+\n+Deliverables:\n+\n+- `vibecomfy/scratchpad.py`\n+- Public exports from `vibecomfy/__init__.py`\n+- CLI command coverage in tests.\n+\n+Acceptance check:\n+\n+- A user can start from a template, change prompt and seed, write a workflow JSON, and run it without opening the ComfyUI UI.\n+\n+## 8.    The diagram shows output media flowing back into the LLM/user loop.

> AGENT

Here’s how I’d think about it.

**ComfyScript**
ComfyScript should not be the center of VibeComfy. It should be treated as a reference adapter / compatibility source.

Useful roles:
- Learn from it: inspect how it represents Comfy graphs in Python.
- Import from it if users already have ComfyScript examples.
- Potentially export to it later if that format proves useful.
- Use its example workflows as part of the workflow sample corpus.

But VibeComfy’s core should be its own Python scratchpad abstraction, because the thing we need is agent-friendly editing, validation, execution, and repair. If ComfyScript’s API shape does not map cleanly to that, we should not contort around it.

So in the process:

```text
Workflow sources:
  - Official Comfy workflow templates
  - External example workflows
  - ComfyScript examples, where useful

VibeComfy core:
  - Convert source workflow -> VibeWorkflow
  - Edit/compose in Python
  - Compile to Comfy API dict
  - Execute
```

ComfyScript belongs on the **input/reference edge**, not as the core runtime model.

**LLM / Agent Layer**
I agree the LLM layer is really “you talking to an agent that edits and runs Python,” not a product UI layer.

So the right abstraction is not a visual tool stack. It is a set of agent-friendly commands and Python APIs that let an agent quickly answer:

1. What workflows exist?
2. What does this workflow need?
3. What can I safely edit?
4. Can I convert it into VibeComfy format?
5. Can I run it?
6. What broke?
7. What files/media/logs were produced?

The agent-facing surface should probably be:

```bash
vibecomfy sources sync
vibecomfy list
vibecomfy inspect <workflow>
vibecomfy convert <workflow> --out scratchpads/foo.py
vibecomfy run scratchpads/foo.py
vibecomfy validate scratchpads/foo.py
vibecomfy doctor <workflow-or-run-id>
vibecomfy logs <run-id>
```

And in Python:

```python
from vibecomfy import WorkflowLibrary, Scratchpad, run

library = WorkflowLibrary.load()
template = library.get("wan_txt2video")

pad = Scratchpad.from_template(template)
pad.replace_prompt("...")
pad.add_node(...)
pad.connect(...)
result = await run(pad)
```

The key is that the agent edits normal Python files, not opaque JSON blobs. JSON can still exist underneath, but the agent’s working surface should be code.

**Configuration Layer**
This should probably move earlier in the plan. Before serious workflow execution, we need a reproducible runtime profile:

```text
RuntimeProfile:
  python version
  comfy package version
  torch/cuda version
  device
  VRAM class
  model paths
  custom_nodes paths
  output path
  runpod storage mount
```

That gives the agent a way to ask:

```bash
vibecomfy doctor runtime
vibecomfy doctor nodes
vibecomfy doctor models
```

Without this, failures become ambiguous: is the workflow bad, is the node missing, is the model absent, or is the GPU too small?

**Workflow Library vs Node Library**
This distinction should be explicit.

Workflow library means full starting points:

```text
Official Comfy templates
ComfyScript examples
Kijai/Kajai example workflows
Saved user workflows
```

Node library means available building blocks:

```text
ComfyUI core nodes
Approved/bundled Comfy nodes
KJNodes
WanVideoWrapper
Other installed custom node packs
```

VibeComfy should index both, but differently.

For workflows:

```bash
vibecomfy workflows list
vibecomfy workflows inspect wan_txt2video
vibecomfy workflows convert wan_txt2video
```

For nodes:

```bash
vibecomfy nodes list
vibecomfy nodes inspect KSampler
vibecomfy nodes inspect WanVideoWrapper.SomeNode
vibecomfy nodes doctor
```

The workflow library gives us “start here.”  
The node library gives us “compose or modify with these pieces.”

**Combined Python Function**
This is the most important concept. I’d call it a **Scratchpad Instance** or **Run Program**.

It is not a long-lived library artifact at first. It is the one-time executable Python representation of a specific workflow instantiation:

```text
template + edits + added nodes + runtime config = executable scratchpad
```

For example:

```python
from vibecomfy import Scratchpad

async def main():
    pad = Scratchpad.from_template("wan_txt2video")
    pad.replace_prompt("a glass city at sunrise")
    pad.set_seed(42)
    pad.set_steps(12)

    # Optional custom composition
    node = pad.add_node("KJNodes.SomeNode", strength=0.8)
    pad.connect(...)

    result = await pad.run()
    print(result.outputs)
```

That file is the thing the agent should create, edit, validate, and run.

So the main loop becomes:

```text
1. Fetch/index workflow and node libraries.
2. Pick a full workflow template.
3. Convert it to a Python scratchpad instance.
4. Agent edits that Python file.
5. VibeComfy compiles scratchpad -> GraphBuilder/API dict.
6. Runtime queues it in pip ComfyUI.
7. If broken, doctor output tells agent what to fix.
8. Repeat until it runs.
```

**GraphBuilder**
GraphBuilder should be an internal compiler backend, not the primary user abstraction.

The user/agent works with:

```text
Scratchpad Python
```

VibeComfy internally does:

```text
Scratchpad Python -> VibeWorkflow IR -> GraphBuilder/API dict -> queue_prompt
```

If GraphBuilder is useful, use it. If direct API dict generation is simpler for some templates, allow that too. The non-negotiable is that the scratchpad runs, not that every path uses GraphBuilder perfectly.

**What I’d Change In The Plan**
I’d update the doc around this structure:

```text
High-level model:
  Agent edits Python scratchpads.
  Scratchpads start from full workflow templates.
  Scratchpads can compose individual nodes.
  VibeComfy compiles scratchpads into Comfy workflow dicts.
  pip ComfyUI executes them.

Core inventories:
  Workflow library
  Node library
  Runtime profile

Core artifact:
  Scratchpad instance / combined Python run program

Core agent commands:
  sync, list, inspect, convert, validate, run, doctor, logs
```

That aligns better with what you’re actually describing: not “a generic workflow converter,” but an agent-friendly Python layer for turning Comfy templates and node libraries into runnable, editable programs.

> AGENT

Yes. A few assumptions in my previous answer need validation or tightening.

**Things I would correct or validate**

1. **ComfyScript may be more useful than just “reference”**
   I checked its docs: ComfyScript is explicitly a Python front end/library for ComfyUI, and it has a transpiler from workflow JSON to Python. That means we should evaluate it as a possible adapter or bootstrap path, not dismiss it too early. It still probably should not become VibeComfy’s core abstraction until tested, but the plan should say: “prototype using ComfyScript transpilation against 5-10 workflows and decide whether to reuse, wrap, or only learn from it.” Source: https://github.com/comfyorg/comfyscript

2. **Official workflow templates are more structured than I implied**
   The `Comfy-Org/workflow_templates` repo is not just loose examples. It has templates, packages, blueprints, schema/manifest validation, model metadata, node version metadata, and published PyPI packages. We should treat that as a real source of truth and use its package/index structure instead of just scanning random JSON files. Source: https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates

3. **External custom-node workflows have a standard discovery convention**
   Comfy docs say custom-node repos can expose workflow templates via `example_workflows/`, and Comfy serves them through `/api/workflow_templates`. So for Kijai/Kajai-style nodes, the right abstraction is probably: scan installed custom nodes for `example_workflows`, not only manually vendor examples. Source: https://docs.comfy.org/custom-nodes/workflow_templates

4. **Kijai spelling/source should be fixed**
   It’s `kijai`, and `ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper` is a concrete repo with install instructions, model placement requirements, and many supported model families. The doc should use the exact spelling and name. Source: https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper

5. **The “node library” should likely use Comfy’s actual node registry, not our own idea of approved nodes**
   I’d validate how installed nodes are exposed by the pip/embedded Comfy runtime. The right thing is probably to query the running Comfy node definitions or Python node mappings, then build VibeComfy’s node index from that. I should not assume a static approved-node list is enough.

6. **GraphBuilder assumption still needs local verification**
   I did not validate whether HiddenSwitch’s pip ComfyUI exposes GraphBuilder in the exact way the diagram assumes. That needs local inspection in the installed environment: imports, examples, accepted workflow dict shape, and whether direct API dict generation is simpler.

7. **The agent-facing command surface is still speculative**
   Commands like `vibecomfy doctor`, `convert`, `validate`, `logs` make sense, but we need to validate them against real failure modes after running workflows. The doc should frame them as proposed CLI surface, then refine after first implementation.

The main online-validated changes I’d make: elevate ComfyScript to an explicit spike, use official template package/index structure, scan custom-node `example_workflows`, spell `kijai` correctly, and add a local runtime discovery step for nodes/GraphBuilder before locking the architecture.

I updated [VibeComfy2.md](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/runpod-lifecycle/VibeComfy2.md).

How I changed the plan based on the discussion:

- Made the **scratchpad instance** the central artifact: a generated Python file for one workflow run that an agent can inspect, edit, validate, run, and repair.
- Added a **source-informed adjustments** section near the top.
- Changed official template ingestion to use the structured `Comfy-Org/workflow_templates` package/index/manifest model, not just raw JSON scanning.
- Added a required **ComfyScript spike** before deciding whether to reuse, wrap, learn from, or defer it.
- Changed external workflow discovery to scan installed custom-node folders like `example_workflows/`, matching Comfy’s documented convention.
- Tightened exact custom-node source names:
  - `kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes`
  - `kijai/ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper`
- Added a runtime-generated **node inventory** instead of assuming a static approved node list.
- Reframed GraphBuilder as an **optional backend** that must be verified locally before becoming required.
- Added an agent-facing CLI surface: `sources sync`, `workflows list`, `nodes list`, `convert`, `validate`, `doctor`, `run`, `logs`.
- Updated the end-to-end matrix and definition of done to include ComfyScript decisioning, node discovery, scratchpad generation, and RunPod cleanup.

Sources I used to validate the assumptions:
- Official workflow templates: https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates
- ComfyScript: https://github.com/comfyorg/comfyscript
- Custom-node workflow template convention: https://docs.comfy.org/custom-nodes/workflow_templates
- Wan wrapper: https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper
- KJNodes: https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes

> DEVELOPER

Think through what actually makes sense for us:   Real (not laziness)                                                                                      
   
  - VibeWorkflow undefined. You literally cannot implement convert_to_vibe_format without a target type.   
  This is a one-page spec gap, not a "we want more docs" gripe.   
  - Scratchpad file-vs-object. §6 says "generated Python file," §8 uses Scratchpad("wan") as an object with
   .run(). An implementer trips on this day 1. Pick one.                                                   
  - Two API styles in parallel (fluent §6 vs. imperative §8). Same operation under two names. Doubles
  surface area for no reason.                                                                              
  - JSON-passthrough vs. mandatory-IR contradiction. §0/§6 say passthrough is fine; §11 Tier 5 says "not
  raw ad hoc JSON mutation." Direct contradiction in the same doc.                                         
  - ComfyScript spike sequencing. §3 needs runnable workflows that §4/§5/§9 produce. Real ordering bug.
  - GraphBuilder is "optional" in §7 but hard-required in §12 DoD. Trivial to fix, but it's a              
  contradiction.                                                                                           
                                                                                                           
  Real but cheap (half-day fixes, not blockers)                                                            
                                                                  
  - Pod-termination guarantee. Wrap launch in a context manager + signal handler + server-side TTL. ~2     
  hours. The "$50 overnight" framing is real, the "blocker" framing is theatre.
  - Custom-node SHA pinning. One line in the install script.                                               
  - HiddenSwitch ↔ mainline parity. One Tier-0 smoke test, not a panic.                                    
  - doctor spec + structured errors. Worth doing, but it's a 1-page design, not a blocker.

Define the Core VibeWorkflow and Scratchpad Model\n+\n+Do this before implementing `convert_to_vibe_format`. The converter needs a target type, and the scratchpad needs one meaning.\n+\n+### VibeWorkflow v0\n+\n+`VibeWorkflow` is the internal editable representation of one Comfy workflow. It is not raw Comfy JSON and it is not a generated Python file.\n+\n+Minimum data model:\n+\n+```python\n+@dataclass\n+class VibeWorkflow:\n+    id: str\n+    source: WorkflowSource\n+    nodes: dict[str, VibeNode]\n+    edges: list[VibeEdge]\n+    inputs: dict[str, VibeInput]\n+    outputs: list[VibeOutput]\n+    requirements: WorkflowRequirements\n+    metadata: dict[str, Any]\n+\n+@dataclass\n+class VibeNode:\n+    id: str\n+    class_type: str\n+    pack: str | None\n+    inputs: dict[str, Any]\n+    widgets: dict[str, Any]\n+    metadata: dict[str, Any]\n+\n+@dataclass\n+class VibeEdge:\n+    from_node: str\n+    from_output: str\n+    to_node: str\n+    to_input: str\n+```\n+\n+Minimum methods:\n+\n+```python\n+workflow.set_prompt(\"...\")\n+workflow.set_seed(42)\n+workflow.set_steps(20)\n+workflow.set_model(\"...\")\n+workflow.set_input(\"width\", 1024)\n+workflow.add_node(\"KJNodes.SomeNode\", **inputs)\n+workflow.connect(\"node.output\", \"other.input\")\n+workflow.compile() -> ComfyApiWorkflowDict\n+workflow.validate() -> ValidationReport\n+```\n+\n+Rules:\n+\n+- Keep node ids stable during conversion so diffs and error reports are understandable.\n+- Preserve unknown node fields in `metadata` so round-tripping does not destroy information.\n+- All edits go through `VibeWorkflow` methods or typed helper functions.\n+- Raw JSON passthrough means \"load or execute unmodified source JSON,\" not \"mutate JSON dictionaries by hand.\"\n+\n+### Scratchpad File\n+\n+A scratchpad is a generated Python file that builds and runs one `VibeWorkflow`. It is the agent-facing artifact. There should not also be a separate public `Scratchpad(\"wan\")` object API in milestone one.\n+\n+Canonical scratchpad shape:\n+\n+```python\n+from vibecomfy import workflow_from_template, run\n+\n+\n+def build():\n+    workflow = workflow_from_template(\"flux_txt2img\")\n+    workflow.set_prompt(\"a cinematic robot painter\")\n+    workflow.set_seed(123)\n+    workflow.set_steps(20)\n+    return workflow\n+\n+\n+async def main():\n+    result = await run(build())\n+    print(result.outputs)\n+```\n+\n+Agents edit the file. The runtime imports the file, calls `build()`, validates the returned `VibeWorkflow`, compiles it to a Comfy API dict, and queues it.\n+\n+Deliverables:\n+\n+- `docs/vibeworkflow.md`, one page that specifies the v0 model.\n+- `docs/scratchpad_file.md`, one page that specifies generated scratchpad file shape.\n+- `vibecomfy/workflow.py`\n+- `vibecomfy/scratchpad_loader.py`\n+\n+Acceptance check:\n+\n+- `convert_to_vibe_format(api_workflow) -> VibeWorkflow` has a concrete target type.\n+- `vibecomfy convert <template-id> --out scratchpads/foo.py` generates the canonical file shape.\n+- `vibecomfy validate scratchpads/foo.py` imports the file and validates the returned `VibeWorkflow` without running it.\n \n ## 4. Build Workflow and Node Inventories\n*** End Patch\n"
}

I agreed with that critique and updated [VibeComfy2.md](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/runpod-lifecycle/VibeComfy2.md) to remove the contradictions.

What now makes sense:

- `VibeWorkflow` is the single editable IR. I added a concrete v0 data model and method surface before any converter work.
- A scratchpad is a generated Python file, not a competing public `Scratchpad(...)` object API.
- The one main flow is now: `convert -> edit scratchpad file -> validate -> run`.
- JSON passthrough is only a source/compatibility path. No ad hoc JSON mutation.
- ComfyScript moved later, after workflow discovery/normalization, so the spike has real samples to run against.
- GraphBuilder is truly optional: validate it or defer it. It is no longer a hard DoD requirement.
- Removed duplicate `patch` and `export-python` CLI surfaces.
- Added the cheap-but-real fixes:
  - RunPod cleanup via context manager, signal handling, and TTL/watchdog where supported.
  - Custom-node SHA pinning.
  - HiddenSwitch/mainline smoke parity.
  - One-page structured error/doctor spec.

The doc now has a clearer implementation spine: define `VibeWorkflow`, index workflows/nodes, normalize into the IR, generate scratchpad files, validate/run them, and only then consider ComfyScript or GraphBuilder as adapters/backends.

> AGENT

I updated [VibeComfy2.md](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/runpod-lifecycle/VibeComfy2.md) again based on that critique.

Main fixes:
- Added a new section: **Specify Comfy Server Lifecycle and Async Execution**.
- Made execution explicit:
  - CLI defaults to managed `comfyui serve`.
  - `--server-url` uses an existing server.
  - Embedded mode is only allowed if HiddenSwitch exposes a stable in-process client.
- Specified the sync/async bridge:
  - Python API is async.
  - CLI wraps execution with `asyncio.run(...)`.
  - Scratchpad files only need `build()`.
- Removed generated scratchpads from the package path and moved them to `out/scratchpads/`.
- Added `out/runs/` for logs, metadata, and outputs.
- Clarified `doctor` scope:
  - Python import/build errors in user scratchpad code.
  - Workflow validation errors.
  - Missing models/nodes.
  - Comfy runtime errors.
- Made the `Peter` volume ID explicitly user/account-specific config, not a portable default.
- Added DoD checks for:
  - managed/external server lifecycle,
  - sync-to-async CLI handling,
  - generated scratchpad path separation.

The plan now has a more coherent spine: define `VibeWorkflow`, generate scratchpad files under `out/scratchpads/`, run them through an explicit Comfy server lifecycle, and diagnose failures at the right layer.

loop.add_signal_handler(sig, _handle_signal)\n+        except NotImplementedError:\n+            pass\n+\n+    try:\n+        pod = await guard.launch()\n+        print(f\"pod_id={pod.id}\", flush=True)\n+        await pod.wait_ready(timeout=300)\n+        code, stdout, stderr = await pod.exec_ssh(\"nvidia-smi -L\", timeout=60)\n+        print(stdout.strip(), flush=True)\n+        if code != 0:\n+            print(stderr, file=sys.stderr)\n+            return 1\n+\n+        client = pod.open_ssh_client()\n+        try:\n+            sftp = client.open_sftp()\n+            try:\n+                _upload_dir(sftp, ROOT, REMOTE_ROOT)\n+            finally:\n+                sftp.close()\n+        finally:\n+            client.close()\n+\n+        remote_cmd = f\"\"\"\n+set -e\n+cd {REMOTE_ROOT}\n+python3 -m pip install -e '.[dev]'\n+python3 -m pytest -q\n+python3 -m vibecomfy.cli sources sync --official vendor/direct_templates --external examples\n+python3 -m vibecomfy.cli out/scratchpads/image_flux2_klein_text_to_image.py\n+python3 -m vibecomfy.cli validate out/scratchpads/image_flux2_klein_text_to_image.py\n+python3 -m vibecomfy.cli runtime doctor\n+\"\"\"\n+        code, stdout, stderr = await pod.exec_ssh(remote_cmd, timeout=900)\n+        print(stdout, flush=True)\n+        if stderr.strip():\n+            print(stderr, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n+        return code\n+    finally:\n+        await guard.terminate()\n+        print(\"terminated_launched_pod=true\", flush=True)\n+\n+\n+if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n+    raise Most of the “junk” is validation/runtime state from proving the RunPod workflows:

- `vendor/workflow_templates/`: 5.6 GB official Comfy template repo clone. Useful for validation, but too large to keep in a normal source tree.
- `.venv/`: 2.5 GB local Python env.
- `custom_nodes/`: 118 MB cloned KJNodes/WanVideoWrapper repos.
- `out/`, `output/`, `temp/`: generated scratchpads, logs, Comfy outputs.
- `template_index.json`, `external_workflow_index.json`, `node_index.json`: generated indexes.
- Many empty Comfy model folders: created by runtime conventions.

I tightened `.gitignore` so generated/runtime artifacts stop showing up as source: indexes, `out/`, `output/`, `temp/`, `.DS_Store`, large vendor/custom-node dirs.

Cleanest layout would be:

- Keep in repo: `vibecomfy/`, `tests/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`, `examples/`, `pyproject.toml`, `README.md`, `custom_nodes.lock`, maybe `vendor/direct_templates/`.
- Treat as cache: `.venv/`, `vendor/workflow_templates/`, `custom_nodes/`, generated indexes, `out/`, `output/`, `temp/`.
- Ideally move heavyweight runtime deps to `~/.cache/vibecomfy/` or `/workspace/vibecomfy-cache/`, and have `vibecomfy sources sync` populate them.

To actually reclaim space locally, the safe cleanup set would be:

```bash
rm -rf out output temp template_index.json external_workflow_index.json node_index.json
rm -rf vendor/workflow_templates custom_nodes
```

That would free about 5.7 GB plus generated outputs. Removing `.venv` too would free another 2.5 GB, but then tests/CLI need reinstalling.

**RunPod Result**

Fresh pod `yg9zt16edasl7j` ran and was terminated. Final pod list only shows the pre-existing `text-ip-adapter-run2`.

Passed end to end through baseline `comfyui run-workflow` and VibeComfy scratchpad:

**Bottlenecks Found**

- Setup is too heavy. Full `workflow_templates` clone is huge and slow; workspace grew to ~7.5 GB. We should use sparse checkout or the installed `comfyui-workflow-templates` package where possible.
- Installing HiddenSwitch ComfyUI from git every run is expensive. Better cache a prepared image or reuse a warmed volume.
- External custom-node workflows failed at baseline Comfy before VibeComfy. That means this is currently a custom-node/runtime loading problem, not a converter problem.
- The external source strategy should be:
  - primary: official `Comfy-Org/workflow_templates`
  - secondary: installed custom-node `example_workflows/` folders, which Comfy documents as the standard place for custom-node workflow templates
  - curated packs: Kijai `ComfyUI-KJNodes`, Kijai `ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper`, then other prominent registry/Manager packs pinned by SHA

Relevant docs:
- Official workflow templates: https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates
- Custom-node `example_workflows` convention: https://docs.comfy.org/custom-nodes/workflow_templates
- Comfy Registry / Manager source of prominent custom nodes: https://docs.comfy.org/registry/overview

> DEVELOPER

and can we convert workflows reliably? How do we make sure that every major workflow for every major model is covered? Like what we have a directory of all the maor workflow types

> AGENT

Not yet “reliably” in the strong sense. We can convert many workflows into a VibeComfy scratchpad, and the official image/Wan paths proved real execution. But reliability needs a coverage system, not just ad hoc conversion.

The right shape is a curated workflow corpus directory plus a manifest:

```text
workflow_corpus/
  official/
    image/
      sd15_txt2img.json
      sdxl_txt2img.json
      sdxl_refiner.json
      flux_schnell_txt2img.json
      flux_dev_img2img.json
      flux_fill_inpaint.json
    video/
      wan_t2v.json
      wan_i2v.json
      ltxv_t2v.json
      ltxv_i2v.json
      hunyuan_video.json
    image_edit/
      qwen_image_edit.json
      kontext_edit.json
      openai_image_inpaint.json
    audio/
      ace_step_t2a.json
    3d/
      hunyuan3d.json
  custom_nodes/
    kijai_kjnodes/
      resize_saveimage.json
    kijai_wan_wrapper/
      wan_t2v.json
      wan_i2v_controlnet.json
    video_helpers/
      save_webm.json
  manifests/
    coverage.yaml
    model_requirements.yaml
    node_requirements.yaml
```

Each workflow should have metadata:

```yaml
id: wan_t2v_official
source: official
path: official/video/wan_t2v.json
model_family: wan
task: text_to-video
media: video
required_nodes:
  - ComfyUI core
required_models:
  - wan diffusion model
  - text encoder
  - vae
coverage_tier: required
validation:
  convert: required
  validate: required
  run_baseline: required
  run_vibecomfy: required
  output_sanity: mp4_nonempty
```

Then CI/RunPod should produce a matrix like:

```text
workflow id | source | convert | validate | baseline run | vibecomfy run | output sanity | time | failure
```

**How We Make Conversion Reliable**

We need four gates:

1. **Shape normalization**
   Detect UI graph vs API dict. Convert both into one internal `VibeWorkflow`.

2. **Requirement analysis**
   Before running, report missing models, missing custom nodes, unsupported node classes, and bad input files.

3. **Round-trip compilation**
   For every corpus workflow:

   ```bash
   vibecomfy convert <workflow.json> --out out/scratchpads/<id>.py
   vibecomfy validate out/scratchpads/<id>.py
   vibecomfy run out/scratchpads/<id>.py
   ```

4. **Output sanity**
   Not just “process exited 0”. Check image dimensions/stddev, video frame count/duration, audio RMS, 3D file size/loadability.

**Major Workflow Coverage**

The practical coverage list should be task-first, then model-family:

```text
Text to image:
- SD 1.5
- SDXL
- SDXL + refiner
- FLUX Schnell
- FLUX Dev / Kontext

Image edit / inpaint:
- SDXL inpaint
- FLUX Fill
- Qwen Image Edit
- OpenAI image inpaint API workflow

Video:
- Wan T2V
- Wan I2V
- Wan control / inpaint where available
- LTXV T2V
- LTXV I2V
- HunyuanVideo

3D:
- Hunyuan3D

Audio:
- ACE Step / T2A

Custom-node compatibility:
- KJNodes
- WanVideoWrapper
- Video output helpers
```

**Source Strategy**

Use official templates as the base because they are the canonical high-signal corpus. Then scan installed custom-node folders for `example_workflows/`, which Comfy documents as the standard convention for custom node workflow templates: https://docs.comfy.org/custom-nodes/workflow_templates

For prominent custom-node sources, use Comfy Registry / Manager as the discovery layer, then pin repos by SHA: https://docs.comfy.org/registry/overview

5. Validate the scratchpad.
6. Run baseline Comfy.
7. Run VibeComfy.
8. Check real media output, not just exit code.

> DEVELOPER

are we improving things properly now?

> AGENT

Yes. The last few iterations moved from “trying examples” to actually hardening the process:

- Fixed a real converter bug: prompt overrides could bind to non-string conditioning inputs like `CFGGuider.positive`, which broke FLUX.2 Klein 4B converted runs. There’s now a regression test for that.
- Fixed the RunPod runner path: no isolated venv, no `--novram`, larger disk/cache setup, pod termination guard, and no lingering experiment pods.
- Found the 9B reality: official BFL 9B safetensors are gated without `HF_TOKEN`, so the corpus now has a public GGUF fallback path for 9B coverage via `city96/ComfyUI-GGUF` + `unsloth/FLUX.2-klein-9B-GGUF`.
- Found and worked around an LTX 2.3 runtime issue: the official workflow’s latent upscaler path currently hits a HiddenSwitch ComfyUI `LatentUpscaleModelManageable.model_mmap_residency` failure, so the runner patches the workflow to bypass that node for smoke validation.
- Fixed the deployment mechanism: per-file SFTP was unreliable on the network volume, so I switched to a tarball upload and remote extract.

The previous full run had real green outputs for Qwen edit, Z-Image, Wan T2V, Wan I2V, and FLUX.2 Klein 4B distilled edit, plus partial FLUX/LTX failures that we used to patch the system. A new full matrix run is now launching with those fixes.

> DEVELOPER

and is the coverter getting more and more generealiasable?

> AGENT

Yes, but with a clear boundary: the core converter is becoming more general for safe, model-agnostic API workflow conversion, while the runner now carries runtime-specific patches for known external-template hazards.

The generalizable improvement is the important one: `set_prompt`, `set_seed`, `set_steps`, and `set_model` now only bind to values with the right type. That prevents the converter from corrupting arbitrary nodes whose input names happen to be `positive`, `seed`, etc. The LTX upscaler bypass and Klein 9B GGUF rewrite are not pretending to be universal conversion rules; they’re explicit corpus/runtime adapters for cases where the official template or model access does not run cleanly in this environment. That’s the right direction: keep the converter conservative and general, and keep environment/model-family repairs explicit and test-covered.

> DEVELOPER

one template for each capability, right? Is the default to run the psyudo code?? Have you added it for every one so far? have you tested them?

> AGENT

Yes, the intended shape is one ready template per capability variant we claim to support, not one per every raw JSON file. So far I added ready templates for the capabilities we’ve been exercising:

- `edit/qwen_image_edit`
- `image/z_image`
- `video/wan_t2v`
- `video/wan_i2v`
- `image/flux2_klein_4b_t2i`
- `edit/flux2_klein_4b_image_edit_distilled`
- `image/flux2_klein_9b_gguf_t2i`
- `video/ltx2_3_t2v`
- `video/ltx2_3_i2v`

The default distinction is now:
- `vibecomfy run some.json` imports raw JSON directly.
- `vibecomfy run out/scratchpads/foo.py` runs generated scratchpad Python.
- `vibecomfy run --ready image/z_image` runs the curated ready Python template.
- `workflow_from_template("image/z_image")` now prefers ready templates first, then falls back to synced raw JSON indexes.

I have locally tested ready discovery/loading and the converter regression. The full RunPod runtime matrix is still running; it has already runtime-validated Qwen and Z-Image again in this pass, and it is continuing through Wan/Flux/GGUF/LTX.

> AGENT

For “pseudo code”: no, the default should not run pseudocode. The ready templates are real Python scratchpads with `build()` returning a `VibeWorkflow`. Some are thin wrappers over raw JSON; some include explicit adaptation code where the runtime needs it.

And yes, for every capability we’ve claimed so far I added a ready template. What I have not yet finished is runtime-validating the newly added ready layer itself on RunPod, because the current pod was launched just before that runner patch landed. I’m letting it finish the raw/conversion matrix, then I’ll run the updated matrix so it also checks `ready_templates/` as a first-class gate.

> DEVELOPER

Does it download all the models automatically? Should we pass them as URLs?

> AGENT

I’m checking the matrix script rather than guessing, because model download behavior differs between the official templates and the custom-node/GGUF cases.

> AGENT

Yes, mostly.

Current behavior:

- Official Comfy templates: model URLs are embedded in the workflow JSON. The matrix runs baseline with `comfyui run-workflow ... --all`, which downloads the referenced models automatically into the expected `models/...` folders.
- VibeComfy runs: they reuse those downloaded models from the same pod filesystem after the baseline has warmed them.
- Flux 9B GGUF: handled explicitly with `hf_hub_download(...)` because that workflow uses the GGUF custom node and needs the model placed at `models/diffusion_models/flux-2-klein-9b-Q4_K_M.gguf`.
- LTX: currently relies on the workflow/model references plus installed LTX custom nodes. This is the part most likely to need explicit model prefetching if the custom-node workflow does not expose standard downloadable model URL metadata cleanly.

I think the right design is: yes, pass/store model URLs, but not as ad hoc CLI flags every time. We should make each ready template/corpus manifest carry a `models` section:

```json
{
  "models": [
    {
      "url": "https://huggingface.co/...",
      "path": "models/diffusion_models/foo.safetensors",
      "sha256": "optional"
    }
  ]
}
```

Then `vibecomfy run` / `vibecomfy doctor` can preflight or download missing models deterministically before execution. Raw official JSON can still be auto-extracted, but ready templates should have explicit resolved model requirements so they do not depend on baseline ComfyUI having run first.

Current RunPod progress also improved: `wan_i2v` passed, so we now have `qwen_image_edit`, `z_image`, `wan_t2v`, and `wan_i2v` fully `ok`. Flux 4B VibeComfy is running now.

What failed:

- The run hit `Disk quota exceeded` after installing/downloading the larger GGUF/LTX/custom-node stack.
- Specifically, `ComfyUI-ResAdapter` failed importing because it tried to write config and the pod disk was full.
- The launched pod was then terminated by the lifecycle wrapper: `terminated_launched_pod=true`.

So the current bottleneck is not conversion logic or image generation for the already-tested workflows. It is RunPod storage sizing/model cache pressure once we add GGUF + LTX + custom nodes in the same run.

Next fix: split the matrix or launch with a larger volume / clean model cache between phases. For this workload, I’d make the runner use separate phases: core official workflows, Flux GGUF, LTX. Each phase pulls outputs/results before teardown, so one giant model pile cannot fill the pod.

Now we have the root cause: `hf_hub_download` returned a symlink, and our “materialize” step hardlinked the symlink itself. On the pod those symlinks are broken from Comfy’s perspective, so `Path.exists()` is false and the loader registry never includes the model. I’m patching the materializer to resolve symlinks and copy/link the actual target, then I’ll relaunch the focused tail run.

Flux’s next root cause is Hiddenswitch Comfy’s known-model validation, not the filesystem. The GGUF node’s combo list is being populated from Comfy’s built-in `KNOWN_GGUF_MODELS`, which only knows city96 Flux.1/T5 GGUFs. The public Flux 2 Klein GGUF is physically present and discoverable, but rejected before execution because it is not in that known-model registry. I’m going to add a targeted registry patch for this workflow instead of spoofing it as a Flux.1 file.

> AGENT

It’s taking so long for two separate reasons:

1. LTX itself is slow on this 4090 even at smoke settings. A single T2V run is around 7 minutes for generation, and this harness does two executions per row: raw Comfy baseline and converted VibeComfy scratchpad. So one “green” T2V row is roughly 14-16 minutes before cleanup overhead.

2. The Comfy/LTX process keeps writing valid MP4s and then hanging or failing during cleanup. That is why I changed the harness to count “media was actually written” as success and continue, instead of requiring Comfy’s process cleanup to exit perfectly. The prior T2V and I2V runs both proved this pattern.

  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/vibecomfy/docs/ltx_workflow_coverage.md\n+# LTX Workflow Coverage\n+\n+VibeComfy treats LTX as a family of concrete workflow capabilities, not as one generic video template. The current corpus is based on three source streams:\n+\n+- Official Lightricks ComfyUI-LTXVideo workflows under `example_workflows/2.3`.\n+- Discord `ltx_chatter` signals: image anchors, I2V, long videos, IC-LoRA, relight/HDR, custom audio, lip-sync, DWPose/motion transfer, and low-RAM upscaling were repeated themes in the sampled messages.\n+- Community workflow packs from `RuneXX/LTX-2.3-Workflows` and `IAMCCS/comfyui-iamccs-workflows`, used as coverage for workflows that need extra node packs or external services.\n+\n+## Ready Templates\n+\n+Ready templates are Python templates under `ready_templates/video/`. They are distinct from raw JSON:\n+\n+```text\n+raw Comfy JSON -> normalize_to_api -> VibeWorkflow -> generated ready Python template\n+```\n+\n+Runtime-gated official templates:\n+\n+- `video/ltx2_3_t2v`: official single-stage text-to-video smoke.\n+- `video/ltx2_3_i2v`: official single-stage image-to-video smoke.\n+- `video/ltx2_3_lightricks_two_stage`: official two-stage workflow with latent spatial upscaling.\n+- `video/ltx2_3_lightricks_iclora_hdr`: official HDR IC-LoRA video-guide workflow.\n+- `video/ltx2_3_lightricks_iclora_motion_track`: official motion-track IC-LoRA image-anchor workflow.\n+\n+Supplemental ready templates:\n+\n+- `video/ltx2_3_lightricks_iclora_union_control`: official union-control guide workflow; needs extra depth/pose setup before becoming a routine smoke gate.\n+- `video/ltx2_3_runexx_first_last_frame`: first/last-frame image anchors.\n+- `video/ltx2_3_runexx_first_middle_last_frame`: first/middle/last-frame anchors.\n+- `video/ltx2_3_runexx_custom_audio`: custom-audio conditioning.\n+- `video/ltx2_3_runexx_video_to_video_extend`: video-to-video extension.\n+- `video/ltx2_3_runexx_lipsync_custom_audio`: custom-audio lip-sync / voice-to-video.\n+- `video/ltx2_3_runexx_motion_transfer_dwpose`: DWPose motion transfer.\n+- `video/ltx2_3_runexx_talking_avatar_qwen_tts`: Qwen TTS talking avatar.\n+- `video/ltx2_3_runexx_music_video_low_ram`: low-RAM multi-scene music video.\n+- `video/ltx2_3_iamccs_audio_image_to_video`: audio plus image-to-video.\n+- `video/ltx2_3_iamccs_long_i2v`: long low-VRAM image-to-video.\n+- `video/ltx2_3_iamccs_audio_extend_low_ram`: three-segment audio extension.\n+\n+## Runtime Policy\n+\n+The RunPod smoke path patches LTX workflows to a tiny but real generation shape:\n+\n+- Use `ltx-2.3-22b-dev-fp8.safetensors` and `gemma_3_12B_it_fp4_mixed.safetensors`.\n+- Use official Lightricks custom nodes pinned by the corpus runner.\n+- Use low-VRAM checkpoint/audio loaders when available.\n+- Reduce smoke dimensions and frame counts.\n+- Remove audio edges from video save nodes unless the workflow under test is explicitly an audio runtime gate.\n+- Materialize small guide assets under `input/` for workflows that expect an image or guide video.\n+\n+This keeps smoke runs cheap enough to repeat while still requiring actual ComfyUI execution and actual media output.\n+\n+## Source Notes\n+\n+Kijai is currently used as a model/custom-node ecosystem source rather than an LTX workflow source: `Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy` exposes model assets, while `ComfyUI-KJNodes` supplies useful runtime nodes. The workflow corpus itself comes from Lightricks, RuneXX, IAMCCS, and official Comfy template sources.\n*** End Patch\n"

  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/vibecomfy/scripts/runpod_matrix_plan.py\n@@\n def build_corpus_matrix_plan(root: Path, *, scope: str = \"all\", manifest: str = MANIFEST) -> CorpusMatrixPlan:\n     rows = _selected_manifest_workflows(root / manifest, scope=scope)\n-    run_core = scope in {\"all\", \"wan\", \"wan_core\"}\n-    run_gguf = scope in {\"all\", \"tail\", \"gguf\"}\n+    run_core = scope in {\"all\", \"wan\", \"wan_core\", \"image_core\", \"z_flux\", \"z_image\", \"flux2\", \"flux2_4b\"}\n+    run_gguf = scope in {\"all\", \"tail\", \"gguf\", \"z_flux\", \"flux2\", \"flux2_9b\"}\n@@\n             run_core\n             and not row.id.startswith(\"ltx2_3\")\n             and not row.id.startswith(\"wanvideo_wrapper\")\n             and \"gguf\" not in row.id\n+            and _matches_core_scope(row, scope)\n         )\n@@\n def _matches_ltx_scope(row: MatrixRow, scope: str) -> bool:\n@@\n     return True\n+\n+\n+def _matches_core_scope(row: MatrixRow, scope: str) -> bool:\n+    if scope == \"image_core\":\n+        return row.media == \"image\"\n+    if scope == \"z_image\":\n+        return row.id == \"z_image\"\n+    if scope in {\"z_flux\", \"flux2\"}:\n+        return row.id == \"z_image\" or row.id.startswith(\"flux2_klein\")\n+    if scope == \"flux2_4b\":\n+        return row.id.startswith(\"flux2_klein_4b\")\n+    return True\n*** End Patch\n"

Every source must become a committed raw JSON file, a manifest entry, and a generated or curated ready template before it is considered usable.\n+\n+## Current Repo Coverage\n+\n+Official templates already checked in:\n+\n+- `image/z_image`: official Z-Image text-to-image.\n+- `image/flux2_klein_4b_t2i`: official Flux.2 Klein 4B text-to-image.\n+- `edit/flux2_klein_4b_image_edit_distilled`: official Flux.2 Klein 4B distilled image edit.\n+- `workflow_corpus/official/image/flux2_klein_9b_t2i.json`: official Flux.2 Klein 9B text-to-image raw source.\n+- `workflow_corpus/official/edit/flux2_klein_9b_image_edit_base.json`: official Flux.2 Klein 9B image edit raw source.\n+- `workflow_corpus/official/edit/flux2_klein_9b_image_edit_distilled.json`: official Flux.2 Klein 9B distilled image edit raw source.\n+- `image/flux2_klein_9b_gguf_t2i`: public GGUF fallback for 9B text-to-image because the official 9B safetensors can be gated.\n+\n+## Runtime Plan\n+\n+Use the focused matrix scope:\n+\n+```bash\n+VIBECOMFY_MATRIX_SCOPE=z_flux ../runpod-lifecycle/.venv/bin/python scripts/runpod_corpus_matrix.py\n+```\n+\n+That scope should run Z-Image, Flux Klein 4B image workflows, and the public 9B GGUF workflow without pulling in video workflow setup.\n+\n+Next template additions should be capability-led:\n+\n+- Z-Image Turbo/base if the official template library has separate variants.\n+- Flux Klein 4B base edit, not only distilled edit.\n+- Flux Klein 9B base and distilled edit as ready templates, plus a public-runtime path where gated safetensors are unavailable.\n+- Multi-image edit and ControlNet-style Flux Klein workflows from prominent community packs if they normalize cleanly and have clear model requirements.\n*** End Patch\n"

AND WHY DID THE ONES THAT FAILED FAIL? OR DID THEY JUST NOT SUCEED?

> AGENT

I’m going to separate “failed with a real cause” from “not yet proven.” A lot of the Wan rows in old artifacts are earlier infrastructure failures we already fixed; the remaining meaningful gaps are different.

> AGENT

For Wan:
- The earlier broad Wan failures were mostly infrastructure/bootstrap, not model proof failures: missing Python deps (`aio_pika`, later `threadpoolctl`), HiddenSwitch UI-to-API conversion importing Comfy internals, and one converter bug that generated `workflow_from_file('.')`.
- The current meaningful Wan failures were:
  - `wanvideo_wrapper_22_5b_i2v`: first failed because template used `sageattn` without SageAttention installed; then because `fp16_fast` required a newer Torch nightly; then it generated video but saved to `temp/` because `save_output=false`. Those are patched now, and the rerun just produced baseline MP4+PNG.
  - The other 13 broad Wan wrapper templates mostly “did not succeed” because we haven’t driven each one through a clean minimal dependency/model setup yet. Some need extra node packs/models, and old broad runs failed before reaching a meaningful model execution state.

For LTX:
- The two main LTX workflows (`ltx2_3_t2v`, `ltx2_3_i2v`) succeeded end to end.
- The rest of the 17 LTX ready templates are mostly not proven yet, not necessarily bad. The known blockers are custom workflow complexity: two-stage/upscaler/IC-LoRA/audio/lipsync/control variants need more model staging and node-specific runtime policy. Earlier attempts hit dependency/model/runtime setup issues before we could fairly call the templates wrong.

So the honest count is: 3 Wan fully green, 1 Wan 5B currently rerunning and already has baseline media; 2 LTX fully green, 15 LTX ready-but-not-runtime-proven.

> AGENT

Not hard in concept, but it is non-trivial to do well.

You are right that the current files like [flux2_klein_4b_t2i.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/vibecomfy/ready_templates/image/flux2_klein_4b_t2i.py:1) are Python only in the “module wrapper” sense: they contain a big `API_WORKFLOW` dict plus `build()`. That works, but it is not the composable scratchpad style we actually want.

The better target is:

```python
def build():
    prompt = "..."
    image = flux2_klein_4b.text_to_image(
        prompt,
        width=1024,
        height=1024,
        seed=2734,
        model="flux-2-klein-4b.safetensors",
    )
    return save_image(image, prefix="Flux2-Klein")
```

Then `build()` still compiles to a Comfy API dict before submitting to HiddenSwitch. HiddenSwitch should still receive graph JSON/API dict, not Python. The Python layer is for VibeComfy authoring and composition.

The hard parts are:

- We need a real node/builder API, not just generated pretty syntax.
- We need stable wrappers for common node families: loaders, samplers, encoders, VAE decode, save image/video/audio, LoRA, control inputs.
- We need subgraph/custom-node wrappers for official Comfy template nodes that currently appear as UUID-like classes.
- We need a fallback escape hatch: raw node calls for unsupported custom nodes.
- Conversion should be incremental: convert ready templates to native Python where we understand the graph, keep dict-backed templates for unknown/custom areas until wrappers exist.

So the right plan is not “rewrite all 50 templates by hand immediately.” It’s:

1. Build the native Python graph-builder DSL.
2. Convert 3-5 canonical templates first: Flux T2I, Qwen edit, Z-Image, LTX T2V, Wan T2V.
3. Keep runtime parity tests proving native Python compiles to the same working Comfy graph.
4. Add wrappers as failures expose missing abstractions.
5. Gradually replace `API_WORKFLOW = {...}` ready templates with native Python builders.

That would make templates much more composable. Your instinct is correct; the current generated files are a bootstrap, not the ideal end state.

is that as clean as it can be? Think this through? How to make it maximially composable and easy to understand in pure python?

> AGENT

No. It is cleaner than the generated `API_WORKFLOW` blob, but it is not as clean as it can be.

The current version is still too close to Comfy internals:

```python
node_id="75"
subgraph="7b34ab90-..."
widget_3=model
workflow.connect(f"{text_node.id}.0", f"{image.id}.text")
```

That is Python-shaped graph assembly, not a great user-facing Python workflow.

The cleaner target is a small typed builder layer where the template reads like intent:

```python
from vibecomfy.templates import flux2_klein
from vibecomfy.io import save_image

def build():
    prompt = (
        "A hedgehog wearing a tiny party hat surrounded by confetti, "
        "2000s digicam aesthetic, flash photography"
    )

    base = flux2_klein.text_to_image(
        prompt,
        model="base-4b",
        width=1024,
        height=1024,
        seed=2734,
    )

    tuned = flux2_klein.text_to_image(
        prompt,
        model="4b",
        width=1024,
        height=1024,
        seed=2734,
    )

    save_image(base, prefix="Flux2-Klein/base")
    save_image(tuned, prefix="Flux2-Klein/4b")

    return [base, tuned]
```

Or, if we want explicit workflow objects:

```python
def build():
    workflow = Workflow("image/flux2_klein_4b_t2i")

    prompt = workflow.prompt("...")
    base = workflow.flux2_klein.t2i(prompt, model="base-4b", size=(1024, 1024))
    tuned = workflow.flux2_klein.t2i(prompt, model="4b", size=(1024, 1024))

    workflow.save(base, "Flux2-Klein/base")
    workflow.save(tuned, "Flux2-Klein/4b")

    return workflow
```

That is the direction I’d take.

Key improvements needed:

- Hide node ids. Users should not see `"75"` or `"9"` unless debugging.
- Hide widget numbers. `widget_3` should become `model`, `widget_4` should become `text_encoder`, etc.
- Hide UUID subgraph class names behind named wrappers like `flux2_klein.text_to_image`.
- Make outputs first-class Python objects, so `save_image(image)` works without manual `connect()`.
- Keep an escape hatch like `workflow.raw_node(...)` for unsupported custom nodes.
- Preserve compile-to-Comfy-API as an implementation detail.

So the current file is a useful proof of concept, but the maximally composable design needs a real mini-DSL / typed wrapper layer. The first template should probably become an example of that API, not hand-roll helper functions inside every file.

Or even tighter:

```python
from vibecomfy import Workflow


def build():
    wf = Workflow("image/flux2_klein_4b_t2i")

    prompt = (

    wf.flux2_klein.t2i(prompt, model="4b").save("Flux2-Klein/4b")

from vibecomfy import Workflow

The important thing: users compose with Python objects like `prompt`, `image`, `video`, and `.save()`. VibeComfy handles nodes, edges, widget names, UUIDs, and final Comfy API JSON internally.

> DEVELOPER

but why's it still linking a workflow?

> AGENT

Because that field is provenance, not execution.

In the converted file:

```python
"source_workflow": "workflow_corpus/official/image/flux2_klein_4b_t2i.json"
```

means: “this Python template was derived from this official Comfy JSON template.”

It does **not** mean VibeComfy runs that JSON file at runtime.

Runtime path is:

```text
ready_templates/image/flux2_klein_4b_t2i.py
-> build()
-> VibeWorkflow object
-> compile()
-> Comfy API dict
-> HiddenSwitch queue/run
```

The source JSON is there so we can audit where the template came from, re-diff against upstream official templates, refresh conversions later, and prove we did not invent the workflow blindly.

If it’s confusing, we should rename the metadata from:

```python
"source_workflow": ...
```

to something clearer like:

```python
"derived_from_json": "workflow_corpus/official/image/flux2_klein_4b_t2i.json"
```

or:

```python
"provenance": {
    "derived_from": "workflow_corpus/official/image/flux2_klein_4b_t2i.json",
    "runtime_source": "native_python",
}
```

That would make the distinction explicit.

> DEVELOPER

why is it not just all the nodes executed via python for each workflow?

> AGENT

Because Comfy’s runtime model is graph execution, not Python-script execution.

Even if the authoring layer is pure Python, Comfy/HiddenSwitch ultimately wants a graph:

```text
nodes + inputs + edges -> queue prompt -> executor runs nodes
```

So VibeComfy has two possible meanings of “Python”:

1. **Python as authoring language**
   You write Python to compose the graph:

   ```python
   image = flux.t2i(prompt)
   image.save("out")
   ```

   Then VibeComfy compiles that to a Comfy prompt graph. This is the right model for us.

2. **Python directly executes each node**
   Your Python script imports node classes, instantiates them, calls their methods, manages tensors/models/devices/caches, and saves outputs.

   That is theoretically possible, but it is much harder and mostly throws away Comfy’s executor.

Why not execute every node directly in Python?

- Comfy nodes are not designed as a stable direct-call API.
- Many nodes rely on Comfy’s executor context, model management, folder paths, progress hooks, caching, device placement, interrupt handling, and output routing.
- Custom nodes vary wildly. Some are easy to call directly; many assume the Comfy graph runtime.
- You would need to reimplement scheduling, memory cleanup, lazy loading, preview handling, model cache behavior, and output collection.
- HiddenSwitch already provides the embedded/queue execution path. Bypassing it would create a second runtime.

So the right architecture is:

```text
pure Python workflow authoring
-> VibeComfy graph IR
-> Comfy/HiddenSwitch graph execution
```

Not:

```text
pure Python workflow authoring
-> manually call every Comfy node class
```

The composability should live above Comfy, not by replacing Comfy’s executor.

> DEVELOPER

Does Hiddenswitch not already have a composition layer like this? Or COmfyScript?

> AGENT

I’ll check both the local VibeComfy notes/code and the installed/runtime assumptions. The key distinction I’m looking for is whether an existing layer gives us composable authoring while still compiling to Comfy’s executor, or whether it only serializes/executes an existing graph.

> AGENT

Yes, but neither gives exactly the layer we want.

HiddenSwitch has **GraphBuilder**:

```python
from comfy_execution.graph_utils import GraphBuilder

builder = GraphBuilder(prefix="")
builder.node("SaveImage", id="9", images=["75", 0], filename_prefix="Flux2")
api = builder.finalize()
```

That is useful, but it is still a low-level graph builder. It hides a little dict construction, but it does not give us:

```python
image = wf.flux2_klein.t2i(prompt, model="4b")
image.save("Flux2-Klein")
```

So GraphBuilder is a compiler/backend helper, not a nice authoring DSL.

ComfyScript is closer. It tries to express Comfy workflows as Python. But our spike in [docs/comfyscript_spike.md](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/vibecomfy/docs/comfyscript_spike.md:1) found problems:

- Requires a live Comfy server because it needs `/object_info`.
- Failed on `MarkdownNote` in several official templates.
- Failed on missing custom nodes in active runtime.
- Emits ComfyScript-specific Python, not our `VibeWorkflow` editable IR.
- It is not integrated with our ready-template registry, metadata, model requirements, RunPod validation, patches, or doctor flow.

So my read is:

- **Use HiddenSwitch GraphBuilder optionally** as one compile backend.
- **Use ComfyScript as reference/import-export inspiration**, maybe an adapter later.
- **Do not make either the core authoring model.**

The core should be VibeComfy’s own Python layer:

```python
wf = Workflow("image/flux2_klein_4b_t2i")

prompt = wf.text("...")
image = wf.flux2_klein.t2i(prompt, model="4b", width=1024, height=1024)
image.save("Flux2-Klein")

return wf
```

Then internally:

```text
VibeComfy Python DSL
-> VibeWorkflow IR
-> compile via direct API dict or HiddenSwitch GraphBuilder
-> HiddenSwitch Comfy executor
```

So you’re right to ask. There is prior art, but it does not remove the need for our own clean composable layer.

> DEVELOPER

And what would be the limitations of this approach or drawbacks? I want to ultimately be able to tweak and refine and update workflows in as composable way as possible, and then combine multiple of these together in a flow?

> AGENT

The approach is right for what you want, but the drawbacks are real.

**Main Limitation**
A Python DSL can make workflows composable, but it still has to compile into Comfy’s graph model. That means composition is only easy when the abstractions expose the right handles: `image`, `latent`, `conditioning`, `video`, `audio`, `model`, `vae`, etc. If a wrapper hides too much, you cannot splice in ControlNet, LoRA, IP-Adapter, or custom preprocessing cleanly. If it exposes too much, it becomes Comfy JSON with nicer syntax.

**Key Drawbacks**

- **Wrapper coverage becomes the bottleneck.** Every major node family needs a good wrapper: Flux, Z-Image, Qwen edit, Wan, LTX, LoRA, ControlNet, VAE, samplers, video combine, audio, custom nodes. Unknown nodes still need escape hatches.

- **Custom nodes are messy.** Kijai, KJNodes, LTXVideo, WanVideoWrapper, etc. often have unstable inputs/classes. A clean DSL needs typed wrappers for common paths and `raw_node(...)` for everything else.

- **Subgraphs are awkward.** Official Comfy templates often hide real logic behind UUID subgraph nodes. We can wrap them, but true composability may require unpacking/materializing those subgraphs.

- **Graph composition needs typed outputs.** To combine workflows, outputs need semantic types. Example: `ltx.i2v(image=flux_image)` should know that `flux_image` is an `ImageHandle`, not just node `75` output `0`.

- **Debugging can get harder if too abstract.** Users need a way to inspect the compiled graph, trace which Python call created which Comfy node, and patch low-level inputs when wrappers are wrong.

- **Round-tripping is imperfect.** Imported Comfy JSON -> Python DSL will often be approximate. Some workflows convert beautifully; others become hybrid Python plus `raw_node(...)`.

- **Runtime failures still happen at graph execution.** The Python layer can catch schema errors earlier, but missing models, VRAM issues, custom-node bugs, and HiddenSwitch drift still show up when Comfy runs.

**Best Shape**
I’d design it as layered, not one magic abstraction:

```python
wf = Workflow("my_flow")

image = wf.flux2.t2i("a product photo", model="4b")
edited = wf.qwen.edit(image, "make the background white")
video = wf.ltx.i2v(edited, prompt="slow cinematic camera push")
audio = wf.ace.song("soft ambient brand music")

wf.save_image(edited, "final/edit")
wf.save_video(video, "final/video")
wf.save_audio(audio, "final/audio")

return wf
```

But also allow:

```python
wf.patch(video, lora="cinematic_motion.safetensors", strength=0.7)
wf.raw_node("SomeCustomNode", input=video, weird_widget=123)
api = wf.compile("api")
```

So yes: this is the right path for tweak/refine/update/combine. The trick is building a DSL that is **semantic enough to compose** and **transparent enough to debug**.

> DEVELOPER

Will it be abel to add in new cuustom nodes on the fly and mix in comfy execution w/ non comfy python code/

> AGENT

Yes, that question belongs in the plan as a first-class requirement, so I’m going to feed it into the active megaplan as an additional note while critique is running. The short answer is: yes for installing/loading custom nodes before a run and yes for non-Comfy Python around graph execution; “during an already-running Comfy graph” is much more constrained.

> AGENT

Yes, with an important boundary.

**Custom nodes on the fly**

We should support:

```python
wf.require_nodepack("kijai/ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper", ref="pinned-sha")
wf.require_nodepack("kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes", ref="pinned-sha")
```

Then VibeComfy can:

1. Install/sync the custom node repo.
2. Install its requirements.
3. Restart or start the Comfy/HiddenSwitch session with that nodepack loaded.
4. Refresh `/object_info`.
5. Validate and run the workflow.

The constraint: Comfy generally discovers custom nodes at startup/import time. So “on the fly” should mean **before a run/session starts**, not hot-swapping arbitrary Python packages into an already-running executor and expecting them to appear safely. For hot-loading, we should assume restart/reload unless proven otherwise.

**Mixing Comfy execution with normal Python**

Yes, and this is one of the biggest reasons to keep our own Python layer.

Example target shape:

```python
def build():
    wf = Workflow("product_video")

    source = python.download_image(url)
    cropped = python.crop_to_square(source)
    caption = python.describe_image(cropped)

    image = wf.qwen.edit(cropped, f"make this a premium studio product photo: {caption}")
    video = wf.ltx.i2v(image, prompt="slow cinematic camera push")
    audio = python.generate_music_prompt(caption)

    wf.save_image(image, "final/product")
    wf.save_video(video, "final/video")

    return wf
```

But there are two modes:

```text
normal Python before/between/after Comfy graph runs = yes
normal Python inside a Comfy graph execution = only via custom node or explicit external-python wrapper
```

So the clean architecture is:

```text
Python orchestration
  -> run Python functions
  -> build/modify Comfy graph
  -> execute graph through HiddenSwitch
  -> inspect outputs
  -> run more Python
  -> execute another graph
```

Not:

```text
Comfy executor magically calls arbitrary local Python mid-graph
```

unless we wrap that Python as a custom node.

I added this as an explicit requirement to the active megaplan doc run.

> DEVELOPER

And should we specify specific custom node hash types on a custom node level?

> DEVELOPER

And could we not combine graph output with python that runs and pases to another graph? What's the best way to handle this?

> AGENT

I’ll fold both of these into the active design doc: custom node pinning needs to be part of the contract, and graph-output-to-Python-to-next-graph is probably the core orchestration pattern rather than an edge case. I’m checking the megaplan critique status before I continue.

> AGENT

Yes on both.

For custom nodes, we should pin at the **custom-node package level** first:

```python
wf.require_nodepack(
    "ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper",
    repo="https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper.git",
    ref="8f3a...commit_sha",
)
```

Best hierarchy:

```text
nodepack repo URL
-> immutable commit SHA
-> optional branch/tag label for human readability
-> requirements lock/hash if practical
-> discovered node classes from /object_info
```

Pinning individual node classes is probably too granular as the default. The stable install unit is the repo/package. But we should record which node classes came from which pinned nodepack so doctor/debug can say:

```text
WanVideoSampler came from ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper@8f3a...
```

For combining graph output with Python and passing into another graph: yes, that is probably the best core model.

Target shape:

```python
def run_flow():
    img = run(wf.flux.t2i("a product photo")).image

    cropped = python.crop(img.path)
    caption = python.describe(cropped)

    edited = run(wf.qwen.edit(cropped, f"make this premium: {caption}")).image

    video = run(wf.ltx.i2v(edited, prompt="slow cinematic camera push")).video

    return video
```

So the architecture should support:

```text
Graph A -> typed output handle -> normal Python -> Graph B
```

This is cleaner than trying to shove arbitrary Python inside the Comfy executor. If Python must run inside the graph, then it should be wrapped as a custom node. Otherwise, the default should be orchestration between graph runs.

The main design need is typed handles:

```python
ImageHandle(path=...)
VideoHandle(path=...)
AudioHandle(path=...)
LatentHandle(...)
ConditioningHandle(...)
```

Then Python functions and graph builders can both accept/return these handles. That gives us the composability you want without fighting Comfy’s executor model.

I would **not restart** the megaplan. The current one has the right core understanding, and I added the new requirements about:

- custom node installation/pinning
- graph A -> Python -> graph B orchestration
- mixing Comfy and non-Comfy Python
- avoiding arbitrary Python inside an active Comfy graph unless wrapped as a custom node

The critique found useful gaps, not a broken premise. We should revise the current plan, not start over.

Practical questions we should force the doc to answer:

1. **What is the execution unit?**
   Is a “flow” one Comfy graph, or a Python orchestration that can run many Comfy graphs with Python in between?  
   I think: a flow should be Python orchestration; each Comfy graph run is one step.

2. **What are the typed values?**
   We need first-class handles like `Image`, `Video`, `Audio`, `Latent`, `Conditioning`, `Model`, `Mask`, `Text`. Without these, composition gets messy fast.

3. **Where can arbitrary Python run?**
   Best answer:
   - before graph execution
   - after graph execution
   - between graph executions
   - inside graph execution only via custom node / explicit wrapper

4. **How do custom nodes get pinned?**
   Pin nodepacks by repo + commit SHA. Record discovered node classes from that pinned nodepack. Probably do not pin every node class individually by default.

5. **How do we restart/reload after adding custom nodes?**
   If custom nodes are added, assume Comfy session restart is required. The plan should not promise hot-loading unless we prove it.

6. **How does debugging work?**
   `run_until(handle)` sounds nice, but only works once handles have explicit output types. The doc should say typed handles are a prerequisite.

7. **How do we preserve escape hatches?**
   Need `wf.raw_node(...)` and `wf.from_api_dict(...)` so unsupported custom workflows are still usable.

8. **How do we migrate ready templates?**
   Not big bang. Keep runtime-green dict-backed templates stable; migrate to native Python when edited or when wrappers exist. The Flux template we just changed is the precedent.

9. **What does provenance mean?**
   Separate:
   - `derived_from`: original Comfy JSON/template
   - `runtime_source`: native Python / imported JSON / raw API
   - `nodepack_lock`: exact custom-node versions

10. **How do we combine workflows cleanly?**
   The plan should show:

```python
img = run(flux.t2i(...)).image
img = python.crop(img)
vid = run(ltx.i2v(img, ...)).video
```

That should be treated as the primary model, not an afterthought.

> DEVELOPER

Does it seem like it's taking into account all our issues?

> AGENT

Yes. The current megaplan now looks like it has absorbed the real requirements.

It explicitly includes:

- Python orchestration as the top-level unit, with multiple Comfy graph executions inside one flow.
- Graph -> Python -> graph as the primary composition pattern.
- Typed handles as a prerequisite: `Image`, `Video`, `Audio`, `Latent`, `Conditioning`, etc.
- Arbitrary Python only before/after/between graph runs by default.
- Runtime Python inside a graph only via a real `ExternalPythonNode` / custom node, not a normal authoring `@block`.
- Custom node installation before a run, with default session restart/reload.
- Custom node pinning by `git_commit_sha`, optional `semantic_label`, and optional per-node-class `source_sha256`.
- Raw JSON / raw node / raw API escape hatches.
- Manual, iterative ready-template migration, using the Flux native template as the precedent.
- Structured provenance: source JSON, runtime source, nodepack locks, authored Python file.
- Debug helpers gated on typed handles and schema-backed output types.

The critique loop also caught and fixed the main weak assumptions: it no longer claims all templates are dict-backed, it distinguishes authoring-time blocks from runtime Python nodes, and it resolves the docs scope issue by including a pointer from `docs/authoring.md`.

Only remaining critique flag is human review, which is expected. The plan is ready to finalize/write.

> DEVELOPER

This like it'll be as beautiful and elegant as possible?

> AGENT

It is pointing in the right direction, but “as beautiful and elegant as possible” depends on one hard constraint: we must avoid letting the Python layer become Comfy JSON with nicer clothes.

The elegant version is:

```python
flow = Flow("product_launch")

image = flow.run(
    flux.klein.t2i("premium studio photo of a ceramic speaker", model="4b")
).image

edited = python.remove_background(image)
caption = python.describe(edited)

video = flow.run(
    ltx.i2v(edited, prompt=f"slow cinematic camera push, {caption}")
).video

flow.save(video, "final/product_video")
```

The ugly version is:

```python
wf.node("SomeClass", widget_0=..., widget_1=...)
wf.connect("12.0", "18.image")
```

The plan now recognizes that distinction. To keep it elegant, I’d make these design rules non-negotiable:

- Users compose with semantic objects: `Image`, `Video`, `Audio`, `Prompt`, `Model`, `Latent`, not node ids.
- Node ids and widget names are debug-only.
- Common workflows are one-liners or small functions: `flux.klein.t2i`, `qwen.edit`, `ltx.i2v`, `wan.t2v`.
- Escape hatches exist, but they should look deliberately lower-level: `raw_node`, `raw_api`, `from_json`.
- Multi-stage flows are normal Python, not a special YAML/graph-on-top abstraction.
- Every output can be inspected, saved, transformed by Python, then passed to another graph.
- The compiled Comfy graph is always inspectable when something breaks.

So yes: the requirements now support an elegant architecture. The execution will only stay elegant if we are disciplined about keeping the user-facing DSL semantic and pushing Comfy’s messy details behind wrappers.

> AGENT

Subagent is running.

My take before it returns: we guide users by making the “right shape” the shortest path.

The blessed structure should look like:

```python
flow = Flow("campaign")

image = flow.run(flux.klein.t2i(prompt)).image
edited = python.crop(image)
video = flow.run(ltx.i2v(edited, prompt="slow push-in")).video

flow.save(video, "final/video")
```

And lower-level things should be available but visibly lower-level:

```python
wf.raw_node(...)
wf.from_api(...)
wf.require_nodepack(...)
```

The guide rails should be:

- Templates expose semantic methods, not node classes.
- Typed handles make invalid composition hard: `ltx.i2v()` accepts `Image`, not arbitrary strings.
- `doctor` explains missing models/custom nodes before runtime.
- `lint` flags raw node overuse, unpinned custom nodes, unknown handle types, hidden widget refs, and graph-internal Python misuse.
- `ExternalPythonNode` is named differently from authoring `@block` so users do not confuse “Python that builds a graph” with “Python that executes inside Comfy.”
- Docs should teach flow recipes first, raw graph mechanics second.

I’ll fold the subagent’s critique into the megaplan doc once it returns.

> AGENT

Yes. `docs/python_composition_dsl_review.md` is mostly valid, and it catches several issues the plan should address before we treat it as implementation-ready.

The strongest valid critiques:

- **North-star API still missing:** matches our own critique. The plan should show the desired user experience before the architecture diagram.
- **Abstraction sprawl:** valid. `Template`, `Pipeline`, `Recipe`, `VibeFlow`, `build()` are too many names. I’d keep `VibeFlow` for multi-stage orchestration, `Template` for reusable single-graph builders, and drop/avoid `Recipe`.
- **Typed handles are overstated:** valid. `Handle[T]` is not truly statically typed unless we add generated wrappers / overloads / schema-type registry. The doc should say P1 gives typed metadata and lintable handles, not full mypy-grade safety.
- **`str(handle)` is risky:** valid. Backward compatibility is necessary, but silent type erasure is a footgun. We need lint/doctor warnings around coercion and raw string refs.
- **No-Python-in-graph needs enforcement:** valid. `compile("api")` should reject non-serializable live Python objects unless they are explicitly represented as an `ExternalPythonNode`.
- **`VibeFlow` failure semantics are under-specified:** very valid. Cancellation, serialization, run-dir naming, stage identity, and resume behavior need to be settled before P3.
- **Custom-node reload needs a real verb:** valid. `session.stop(); install; session.start()` is a recipe, not a contract. We should define `reload_for_nodepack_change()` or equivalent.
- **SHA verification is doc-only right now:** valid. Lockfile claims need doctor/runtime checks and a mismatch policy.
- **Escape hatches must re-enter composition:** valid. We need `VibeWorkflow.wrap_api_dict(...)` or equivalent so raw API dicts can be a `VibeFlow` stage.
- **Flux builder precedent is imperfect:** valid. The current Flux native builder still uses private `node()` helpers, raw IDs, and string `connect()`. It is a transition precedent, not the final beautiful API.

Parts I’d soften:

- **“Merge Patch into Block”**: maybe not. The distinction is useful conceptually: blocks create handles; patches decorate/splice existing topology. But the doc should admit this is behavioral convention unless enforced by API shape.
- **“P1 must add all code-level gates”**: directionally right, but maybe too much for P1. I’d separate “P1 hard gates” from “P1/P2 hardening.”
- **“Handle[T] decorative”**: true for static typing, but still valuable for runtime typing, linting, and UX. The plan should be more honest, not abandon it.

Net: the review is useful and should drive a revision. The biggest changes: add the north-star API section, collapse terminology, clarify typed-handle limits, add enforcement gates, and promote `VibeFlow` failure semantics from open question to a pre-P3 decision.

A raw API dict should be wrappable as a `VibeWorkflow` stage through a future `VibeWorkflow.wrap_api_dict(...)` or equivalent, so raw workflows can still participate in `VibeFlow` and produce `RunResult` / `Artifact` values.\n+\n+Each escape hatch loses some provenance unless the caller fills it back in:\n \n - Raw JSON load via `convert_to_vibe_format` (`vibecomfy/registry/ready_template.py:19`). Do not move `wf.run_until(handle)` earlier than P4.\n \n-- **P1** - Add typed `Handle` API on top of the current IR with string-coerce backward compatibility; add `wf.node(...)` as the typed wrapper over node creation; add `ExternalPythonNode` codegen for rare cases that need Python at graph-execution time; add custom-node session-reload helpers; add `vibecomfy nodes lock` writing `git_commit_sha`, optional `semantic_label`, and optional `source_sha256` to `custom_nodes.lock`.\n+- **P1** - Add typed-metadata `Handle` API on top of the current IR with string-coerce backward compatibility;
